First, we factor the denominator:

$$
\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {cos}^{3}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta {sin}^{3}⁡\theta }=\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}
$$

Next, we use the Pythagorean identity to rewrite the expression in the parentheses, and then we simplify the resulting expression as much as possible.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )} & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {cos}^{3}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta {sin}^{3}⁡\theta }=\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .
$$
